Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when required content genuinely needs the space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via its sync procedure; re-apply or retire logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when required content genuinely needs the space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via its sync procedure; re-apply or retire logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

</system-reminder>

107	/** Collects folded SSE events from `/runs/:id/events` as they arrive. */
108	function collectSse(port: number, runId: string): {
109	  close: () => void
110	  waitForCount: (n: number, timeoutMs?: number) => Promise<FeedEvent[]>
111	} {
112	  const events: FeedEvent[] = []
113	  let buffer = ''
114	  const waiters: { n: number; resolve: (value: FeedEvent[]) => void }[] = []
115	  const req = httpGet(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/runs/${runId}/events`, (res) => {
116	    res.setEncoding('utf8')
117	    res.on('data', (chunk: string) => {
118	      buffer += chunk
119	      let boundary = buffer.indexOf('\n\n')
120	      while (boundary !== -1) {
121	        const frame = buffer.slice(0, boundary)
122	        buffer = buffer.slice(boundary + 2)
123	        const dataLine = frame.split('\n').find(candidate => candidate.startsWith('data: '))
124	        if (dataLine !== undefined) {
125	          events.push(JSON.parse(dataLine.slice('data: '.length)) as FeedEvent)
126	          for (const waiter of waiters.splice(0, waiters.length)) {
127	            if (events.length >= waiter.n) waiter.resolve(events.slice())
128	            else waiters.push(waiter)
129	          }
130	        }
131	        boundary = buffer.indexOf('\n\n')
132	      }
133	    })
134	  })
135	  const waitForCount = (n: number, timeoutMs = 4_000): Promise<FeedEvent[]> => new Promise((resolvePromise, reject) => {
136	    if (events.length >= n) {
137	      resolvePromise(events.slice())
138	      return
139	    }
140	    const timer = setTimeout(() => { reject(new Error(`timed out waiting for ${n} SSE events; got ${events.length}`)) }, timeoutMs)
141	    waiters.push({ n, resolve: (value) => { clearTimeout(timer); resolvePromise(value) } })
142	  })
143	  return { close: () => { req.destroy() }, waitForCount }
144	}

1	/**
2	 * Generates the customer proof-of-concept's 147-agent enterprise roster from
3	 * sources this repository actually defines: package READMEs, `verify-*`
4	 * scripts, CI gate names, Agent Notes, skill directories, and recorded bench
5	 * fixtures. Every {@link RosterAgentDefinition.source} is a repository-relative
6	 * path this generator checks with `existsSync` before emitting it, so a
7	 * renamed or removed source fails the generator loudly instead of shipping a
8	 * roster entry nothing backs.
9	 *
10	 * The roster is a composition of role x division x specialization: each
11	 * division below builds its slice from one real, enumerable pool (a package
12	 * group's leaves, a directory of `verify-*.ts` scripts, the CI gate union in
13	 * `run-gates.ts`, an Agent Note class, a skill directory, or a recorded bench
14	 * scenario) so the entry count is a design constant while the cited source is
15	 * discovered, not hand-typed per entry. Pool iteration order is `Array#sort`
16	 * on the pool's own keys, which is what makes the output byte-identical for
17	 * the same tree.
18	 *
19	 * `status` here is always `"defined"` and `counts.active` is always `0`: this
20	 * module describes what the repository defines, never what is running. Live
21	 * status and active counts are computed by `scripts/harness-feed.ts` from real
22	 * session data and are never written back into this file.
23	 *
24	 * @module enterprise-roster
25	 */
26

28	import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
29	import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path'

32	/** One LLM route: the provider a Service Definition registers plus the model id it accepts. */

34	  /** Provider route key (e.g. `deepseek-official`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `openrouter`). */
35	  provider: string
36	  /** Model id sent to that provider. */
37	  model: string
38	}

40	/** One roster entry: a defined agent seat, grounded in one real repository source. */
41	export interface RosterAgentDefinition {
42	  /** Unique, kebab-case, stable across regenerations while its source stays put. */
43	  id: string
44	  /** Human-readable name for display. */
45	  name: string
46	  /** The agent's function (e.g. `steward`, `reviewer`, `verifier`, `judge`, `curator`). */
47	  role: string
48	  /** The division id this agent belongs to; matches one entry in {@link Roster.divisions}. */
49	  division: string

57	  preset: string

59	  skills: string[]

72	 * `merges` (an integrator merges a department's findings), `reads` (a curator

115	/**
116	 * Resolve one hardcoded relative source path against the repository root and
117	 * fail loudly if it is missing, instead of shipping a roster entry nothing on
118	 * disk backs.
119	 * @param root - repository root.
120	 * @param relative - repository-relative path (forward slashes) to cite.
121	 * @returns `relative`, unchanged, once existence is confirmed.
122	 */
123	function cite(root: string, relative: string): string {
124	  if (!existsSync(join(root, relative))) {
125	    throw new Error(`enterprise-roster: cited source "${relative}" does not exist in this tree`)
126	  }
127	  return relative
128	}

130	/**
131	 * Real leaf package directories (each with its own `README.md`) directly
132	 * under one package group, sorted for deterministic iteration.
133	 * @param root - repository root.
134	 * @param group - group directory name under `packages/`.
135	 * @returns sorted leaf directory names.
136	 */
137	function packageLeaves(root: string, group: string): string[] {
138	  const dir = join(root, 'packages', group)
139	  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })
140	    .filter(entry => entry.isDirectory())
141	    .map(entry => entry.name)
142	    .sort()
143	}

145	/**
146	 * Real `verify-*.ts` gate scripts (excluding their `.spec.ts` tests), sorted
147	 * for deterministic iteration.
148	 * @param root - repository root.
149	 * @returns sorted script filenames under `scripts/`.
150	 */
151	function verifyScripts(root: string): string[] {
152	  return readdirSync(join(root, 'scripts'))
153	    .filter(name => name.startsWith('verify-') && name.endsWith('.ts') && !name.endsWith('.spec.ts'))
154	    .sort()
155	}

157	/**
158	 * Real recorded bench scenario directories under the headless-agent example's
159	 * snapshot suites, sorted for deterministic iteration.
160	 * @param root - repository root.
161	 * @returns sorted `examples/headless-agent/tests/...` scenario paths.
162	 */
163	function provingGroundScenarios(root: string): string[] {
164	  const bases = [
165	    'examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots',
166	    'examples/headless-agent/tests/workspace-context-resume-snapshots',
167	    'examples/headless-agent/tests/semantic-checkpoint-snapshots',
168	  ]
169	  const scenarios: string[] = []
170	  for (const base of bases) {
171	    const abs = join(root, base)
172	    if (!existsSync(abs)) continue
173	    for (const entry of readdirSync(abs, { withFileTypes: true })) {
174	      if (entry.isDirectory()) scenarios.push(`${base}/${entry.name}`)
175	    }
176	  }
177	  return scenarios.sort()
178	}

180	/** Real `.agents/skills/<id>` directories, sorted for deterministic iteration. */
181	function skillDirectories(root: string): string[] {
182	  return readdirSync(join(root, '.agents/skills'), { withFileTypes: true })
183	    .filter(entry => entry.isDirectory())
184	    .map(entry => entry.name)
185	    .sort()
186	}

188	/** Convert a kebab-case slug into a Title Case display name. */
189	function titleCase(slug: string): string {
190	  return slug.split('-').map(word => word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1)).join(' ')
191	}

193	/**
194	 * The source tree's latest commit timestamp, which is what keeps
195	 * {@link Roster.generatedAt} stable across regenerations of the same tree. A
196	 * tree with no git history (e.g. an exported tarball) falls back to a fixed
197	 * epoch instead of the wall clock, which would break idempotency.
198	 * @param root - repository root.
199	 * @returns ISO 8601 commit timestamp, or the fixed fallback.
200	 */
201	function generatedAt(root: string): string {
202	  return tryGitCommitDate(root) ?? '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z'
203	}
204	
205	/** @returns the HEAD commit's committer date, or `undefined` when git metadata is unavailable. */
206	function tryGitCommitDate(root: string): string | undefined {
207	  try {
208	    return execFileSync('git', ['log', '-1', '--format=%cI'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' }).trim() || undefined
209	  } catch {
210	    // No git metadata reachable (a tarball export, or a shallow clone with no
211	    // commits checked out) — generatedAt falls back to a fixed timestamp.
212	    return undefined
213	  }
214	}

1	# Enterprise roster
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	`roster.json` in this directory is a generated, 147-agent roster for the enterprise proof of concept: a composition of role x division x specialization built from sources this repository actually defines. [`scripts/enterprise-roster.ts`](../../scripts/enterprise-roster.ts) generates it (`pnpm run roster`); [`scripts/harness-feed.ts`](../../scripts/harness-feed.ts) serves it with live status overlaid (`pnpm run feed`).
6	
7	## The honesty rule
8	
9	147 is the count of agents this repository **defines** — every entry's `source` field names a real, existing repository path (a package README, a `verify-*.ts` script, a CI gate name, an Agent Note, a skill directory, or a recorded bench scenario), checked against disk when the roster is generated. It is never the count of agents currently running. `counts.active` in the committed file is always `0`, and every agent's `status` is always `"defined"`.
10	
11	Live status comes only from `GET /roster` on the running feed (`pnpm run feed`), which overlays the committed roster with what real session data on disk says right now: an agent is `active` while a discovered run has a session mapped to it and still running, `certified` once that session logs a certificate-shaped event, and `failed` if its run ended without one. An agent with no matching session keeps `"defined"`. A fresh checkout, with no `.proving-ground/`, `data/proving-ground/`, or `.code-safety/` runtime data yet, reports `active: 0` for all 147 — that is the correct, honest answer, not a bug.
12	
13	## Divisions
14	
15	| Division | Purpose |
16	|---|---|
17	| `harness-core` | Stewards the product API spine: session, prompt assembly, tools, agent, the agent loop, LLM routing, and subagent delegation. |
18	| `proving-ground` | Operates the harness against real bench scenarios recorded under `examples/headless-agent/tests`. |
19	| `verification` | Runs the `verify-*` scripts that gate changed source before it ships. |
20	| `judging` | Decides pass or fail at each named CI gate. |
21	| `curation-data` | Curates the Agent Note corpus and fixture datasets, and keeps score of usage for the observatory. |
22	| `program-departments` | Coordinates cross-cutting package groups as departments of one program. |
23	| `code-safety` | Reviews target repositories for secrets, injection, access, data, dependency, and platform risk, per language. |
24	| `knowledge` | Keeps the repository's reusable skills current and discoverable. |
25	| `governance` | Owns process standards: labels, stacking, dependencies, vendoring, licensing, and translation pairing. |
26	| `observatory` | Watches session telemetry, token spend, and query surfaces across runs. |
27	
28	## Code-safety specializations name a target, not an implemented scanner
29	
30	This repository is TypeScript/JavaScript and ships no Java, Go, PHP, or mobile static-analysis tooling. Every department x specialization reviewer seat — including the four languages this repository does not implement a scanner for — cites its department's real grounding package (credentials, shell, filesystem, storage, license verification, or sandbox policy); the specialization records what the seat is *for*, not a claim that a matching scanner already runs. Read [`scripts/enterprise-roster.ts`](../../scripts/enterprise-roster.ts) for exactly which source grounds each department, and the [Agent Note](../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-19-enterprise-roster-and-harness-feed.md) for the full rationale.
31	
32	## Regenerating

34	```sh
35	pnpm run roster
36	```

38	The generator is idempotent: run against an unchanged tree, it reproduces `roster.json` byte for byte. A diff after a clean regeneration means a cited source moved; the generator's own error, thrown before it writes anything, names which one.

1	# 企业花名册
2	
3	[English](README.md) | 中文
4	
5	本目录下的 `roster.json` 是为企业概念验证生成的、包含 147 个智能体的花名册：由本仓库真实定义的来源构建出的"角色 x 事业部 x 专精方向"组合。[`scripts/enterprise-roster.ts`](../../scripts/enterprise-roster.ts) 生成该文件（`pnpm run roster`）；[`scripts/harness-feed.ts`](../../scripts/harness-feed.ts) 在其上叠加实时状态后提供服务（`pnpm run feed`）。
6	
7	## 诚实原则
8	
9	147 是本仓库**已定义**的智能体数量——每条记录的 `source` 字段都指向一个真实存在的仓库路径（一个包 README、一个 `verify-*.ts` 脚本、一个 CI 关卡名称、一份 Agent Note、一个技能目录，或一个已记录的基准场景），并在生成花名册时对照磁盘做过校验。它绝不是当前正在运行的智能体数量。已提交文件中的 `counts.active` 始终为 `0`，且每个智能体的 `status` 始终为 `"defined"`。
10	
11	实时状态只来自正在运行的 feed 上的 `GET /roster`（`pnpm run feed`），它会用磁盘上真实会话数据当下反映的情况,叠加到已提交的花名册上：当某次已发现的运行中存在一个映射到该智能体、且仍在运行的会话时，状态为 `active`；一旦该会话记录了一个证书形状的事件，状态变为 `certified`；若其所属运行已结束但未记录该事件，则为 `failed`。没有匹配会话的智能体保持 `"defined"`。一次全新检出、尚无 `.proving-ground/`、`data/proving-ground/` 或 `.code-safety/` 运行时数据时，全部 147 个智能体都会报告 `active: 0`——这是正确、诚实的答案，而不是缺陷。
12	
13	## 事业部
14	
15	| 事业部 | 职责 |
16	|---|---|
17	| `harness-core` | 守护产品 API 主干：会话、提示词组装、工具、智能体、智能体循环、LLM 路由与子智能体委派。 |
18	| `proving-ground` | 让 harness 在 `examples/headless-agent/tests` 下记录的真实基准场景中运行。 |
19	| `verification` | 运行在源码变更上线前把关的 `verify-*` 脚本。 |
20	| `judging` | 在每个命名的 CI 关卡上裁定通过或失败。 |
21	| `curation-data` | 整理 Agent Note 语料库与夹具数据集，并为观测台记录用量分数。 |
22	| `program-departments` | 将横切的软件包分组协调为同一项目下的各部门。 |
23	| `code-safety` | 按语言审查目标仓库中的密钥、注入、访问、数据、依赖与平台风险。 |
24	| `knowledge` | 让仓库中可复用的技能保持最新且易于发现。 |
25	| `governance` | 掌管流程标准：标签、堆叠、依赖、代码引入、许可与翻译配对。 |

29	
30	本仓库是 TypeScript/JavaScript 项目，并未提供 Java、Go、PHP 或移动端的静态分析工具。每一个"部门 x 专精方向"审查席位——包括本仓库未实现扫描器的四种语言——都引用其所属部门真实的依托软件包（凭证、Shell、文件系统、存储、许可证校验或沙箱策略）；专精方向记录的是该席位*为何而设*，而非声称已有匹配的扫描器在运行。具体是哪个来源支撑了每个部门，请参阅 [`scripts/enterprise-roster.ts`](../../scripts/enterprise-roster.ts)；完整理由参阅 [Agent Note](../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-19-enterprise-roster-and-harness-feed.md)。

1	# Agent Note: The enterprise roster is generated from real sources; the feed computes liveness, never invents it
2	
3	Status: implemented
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-19-enterprise-roster-and-harness-feed.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A customer proof of concept needs to present a large, structured "enterprise" of agents — divisions, departments, specializations — without pretending the harness runs 147 concurrent agents today. Two failure modes were both live risks: a hand-authored roster JSON that drifts from the repository the moment a package is renamed or removed, and a status field that reports "active" for seats nothing is actually running. Either one turns a proof of concept into a fabrication the first time someone checks it against the repository.
10	
11	## Decision
12	
13	**The roster is generated, not authored, and every entry cites a real, checked path.** `scripts/enterprise-roster.ts` composes exactly 147 agents as role x division x specialization, where each division's slice is built from one enumerable, real pool: `packages/core`, `packages/llm`, and `packages/subagent` leaf directories for `harness-core`; recorded bench scenarios under `examples/headless-agent/tests/*snapshots*` for `proving-ground`; `scripts/verify-*.ts` for `verification`; the CI gate ids in `scripts/run-gates.ts` for `judging`; `.agents/notes/implemented/<class>` directories plus the token-meter package for `curation-data`; ten package group READMEs for `program-departments`; six department-grounding packages crossed with six language specializations for `code-safety`; `.agents/skills/<id>` directories for `knowledge`; eight process-standard files for `governance`; and six telemetry/query sources for `observatory`. A `cite()` helper resolves every hardcoded relative path against `existsSync` before the generator emits it, so a renamed or deleted source fails the generator immediately, naming the missing path, rather than shipping a roster entry nothing backs.
14	
15	**`generatedAt` is the tree's last commit timestamp, not the wall clock.** Reading `git log -1 --format=%cI` instead of `Date.now()` is what makes `buildRoster()` produce byte-identical JSON on repeated runs against the same commit — a real idempotency property, not merely a stable field count. A tree with no git history falls back to a fixed epoch rather than breaking the guarantee.
16	
17	**The generated file's `status` is always `"defined"` and `counts.active` is always `0`.** This module describes what the repository defines; it has no session data and must not guess. `scripts/harness-feed.ts` is the only place liveness is computed: its `GET /roster` handler reads the committed roster, then maps each agent to a live session (best-effort, by preset id and role/department keywords present in the session's stamped `request/header` and `tool/call` data) to decide `active` (a matching session is open), `certified` (that session logged a `verification/certificate`-shaped event before ending) or `failed` (it ended without one), and only then are the counts recomputed. The committed file and the served response are never the same object; the served response is derived and discarded per request.
18	
19	**Code-safety specializations name a target, not an implemented scanner.** This repository is TypeScript/JavaScript and has no Java, Go, PHP, or mobile static-analysis tooling, so every one of the 36 department x specialization reviewer seats cites its department's real grounding package (`dsh-credentials`, `dsh-shell`, `dsh-fs`, `dsh-storage`, the license-verification script, `dsh-sandbox`) regardless of which language the seat names; the specialization records what the seat is *for*, and `data/enterprise/README.md` states this plainly so a reader does not mistake "defined" for "implemented."
20	
21	**The event fold in `harness-feed.ts` is written against the real session-event vocabulary, not the aspirational one.** `packages/core/session` defines `turn/start`, `turn/end`, `step/start`, `step/end`, `tool/call`, `tool/result`, `assistant/message`, and `agent/inbox/spliced`; there is no `agent/step`, `subagent/*`, `program/delegation`, `program/integration`, or `verification/certificate` event type in this tree today. The fold maps the real types (`turn/*` and `step/*` to `step`; `tool/call`/`tool/result` to `tool`, or to `delegation` when the tool name is one of the subagent tools; `agent/inbox/spliced` to `directive`) and additionally recognizes the aspirational prefixes (`verification/certificate` to `certificate`, `program/integration` to `merge`, a `finding`-prefixed type to `finding`, a denial-shaped tool failure to `refusal`) so that when the parallel proving-ground and code-safety programs start emitting those events, the fold requires no change. An event type the fold does not recognize is dropped from the stream, never a crash and never a placeholder record.
22	
23	## Consequences
24	
25	- `pnpm run roster` regenerates `data/enterprise/roster.json` deterministically; a diff in that file after a clean regeneration means a cited source moved, and the generator's own error names which one.
26	- `pnpm run feed` serves `GET /roster`, `GET /runs`, `GET /runs/:id/events` (SSE), `GET /safety/:id`, and `POST /safety` on port 4711 (`--port` to override) or against a `--fixtures <dir>` directory for the front end's own tests; it discovers `.proving-ground/runs/*`, `data/proving-ground/*/sessions/*.jsonl`, and `.code-safety/*` at request time and tolerates all three being absent, which they are in a fresh checkout — these are runtime output directories, not repository fixtures.
27	- `POST /safety` returns 501 until the parallel code-safety workstream lands `pnpm run code-safety`; the feed checks for that script in `package.json` on every request rather than caching its absence, so the 501 clears the moment the script is added with no feed change required.
28	- The honesty rule this note exists to enforce: 147 is always the defined count; the active count is whatever `GET /roster` computes from real session directories at the moment of the request, including zero.
29	
30	## Alternatives considered
31	
32	- **Hand-authoring `roster.json` once and committing it as static data** — the first package rename or removal would silently strand entries pointing at nothing, with no mechanism to notice. Generation with a checked `cite()` turns that into a build failure instead of a silent lie.
33	- **Wall-clock `generatedAt`** — makes every regeneration a diff even when nothing sourced from the tree changed, which defeats the point of an idempotency check.
34	- **Reusing the fictional event names (`agent/step`, `program/integration`) as the fold's primary keys** — would make the fold's happy path untestable against any session log this repository can currently produce. Folding the real vocabulary first, with the aspirational names as additional recognized prefixes, keeps the keyless test suite exercising real behavior while staying forward-compatible.
35	- **Treating a missing `.proving-ground/`, `data/proving-ground/`, or `.code-safety/` as an error** — these are runtime directories the parallel workstreams populate on a real machine; a fresh checkout or CI runner without them is the common case, not a misconfiguration.
36

35	  version: number
36	  id: SessionId
37	  createdAt: number
38	  cwd?: string
39	  parentSession?: SessionId
40	  seedLength?: number
41	  origin?: 'subagent'
42	  delegationDepth: number
43	  agentPreset?: string

46	/**
47	 * Build the header line object from a {@link SessionHeader}.
48	 * @param header - the immutable session metadata to serialize.
49	 * @returns the `type: 'session'`-tagged line object, absent optional fields omitted (never null).
50	 */
51	export function toHeaderLine(header: SessionHeader): HeaderLine {
52	  return {
53	    type: 'session',
54	    version: header.version,
55	    id: header.id,
56	    createdAt: header.createdAt,
57	    ...header.cwd !== undefined ? { cwd: header.cwd } : {},
58	    ...header.parentSession !== undefined ? { parentSession: header.parentSession } : {},
59	    ...header.seedLength !== undefined ? { seedLength: header.seedLength } : {},
60	    ...header.origin !== undefined ? { origin: header.origin } : {},
61	    delegationDepth: header.delegationDepth ?? 0,
62	    ...header.agentPreset !== undefined ? { agentPreset: header.agentPreset } : {},
63	  }
64	}
65	
66	/**
67	 * Parse a header line back into a {@link SessionHeader}.
68	 * @param line - the shape-checked first line of a log (see the `isHeaderLine` guard).
69	 * @returns the header, absent optional fields omitted.
70	 */
71	export function fromHeaderLine(line: HeaderLine): SessionHeader {
72	  if (Object.hasOwn(line, 'sandboxMode') || Object.hasOwn(line, 'approvalPolicy')) {
73	    throw new Error('session header uses retired policy baseline fields')
74	  }
75	  return {
76	    version: line.version,
77	    id: line.id,
78	    createdAt: line.createdAt,
79	    ...line.cwd !== undefined ? { cwd: line.cwd } : {},
80	    ...line.parentSession !== undefined ? { parentSession: line.parentSession } : {},
81	    ...line.seedLength !== undefined ? { seedLength: line.seedLength } : {},
82	    ...line.origin !== undefined ? { origin: line.origin } : {},
83	    delegationDepth: line.delegationDepth,
84	    ...line.agentPreset !== undefined ? { agentPreset: line.agentPreset } : {},
85	  }
86	}

88	/** Type guard: a parsed first line is a well-formed session header. */
89	function isHeaderLine(value: unknown): value is HeaderLine {
90	  return (
91	    typeof value === 'object' && value !== null
92	    && (value as { type?: unknown }).type === 'session'
93	    && typeof (value as { version?: unknown }).version === 'number'
94	    && typeof (value as { id?: unknown }).id === 'string'
95	    && typeof (value as { createdAt?: unknown }).createdAt === 'number'
96	    && Number.isSafeInteger((value as { createdAt: number }).createdAt)
97	    && (value as { createdAt: number }).createdAt >= 0
98	    && !Object.is((value as { createdAt: number }).createdAt, -0)
99	    && typeof (value as { delegationDepth?: unknown }).delegationDepth === 'number'
100	    && Number.isSafeInteger((value as { delegationDepth: number }).delegationDepth)
101	    && (value as { delegationDepth: number }).delegationDepth >= 0
102	    && !Object.is((value as { delegationDepth: number }).delegationDepth, -0)
103	    && ((value as { origin?: unknown }).origin === undefined
104	      || (value as { origin?: unknown }).origin === 'subagent')
105	    && ((value as { agentPreset?: unknown }).agentPreset === undefined
106	      || typeof (value as { agentPreset?: unknown }).agentPreset === 'string')
107	  )
108	}
109	
110	/**
111	 * Encode an arbitrary string as a single safe path segment, injectively over ALL JS (UTF-16)
112	 * strings — including lone surrogates. A {@link SessionId} is an unvalidated branded string,
113	 * so this neutralizes `../`, absolute paths, NUL, and separators before any filesystem use.
114	 * Safe code units remain literal; every other unit, including `~`, becomes
115	 * `~XXXX`. Operating on code units preserves lone surrogates, while special-
116	 * casing `.` and `..` prevents traversal by an otherwise safe whole segment.
117	 *
118	 * @param raw - the string to encode; must be non-empty (throws on `''`).
119	 * @returns the escaped single path segment, decodable back to `raw`.
120	 */
121	export function encodeSegment(raw: string): string {
122	  if (raw.length === 0) throw new Error('cannot encode an empty path segment')
123	  if (raw === '.') return '~002E'
124	  if (raw === '..') return '~002E~002E'
125	  let out = ''
126	  for (let i = 0; i < raw.length; i++) {
127	    const code = raw.charCodeAt(i)
128	    const ch = String.fromCharCode(code)
129	    if (ch !== '~' && /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]$/.test(ch)) {
130	      out += ch
131	    } else {
132	      out += '~' + code.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(4, '0')
133	    }
134	  }
135	  return out
136	}
137	
138	/**
139	 * Build the readable directory key for a project path.
140	 * Filesystem separators and drive separators become `-`; unsafe code units use
141	 * the same `~XXXX` escape as session ids. The key is bounded for filesystem
142	 * component limits. Separator replacement and truncation are intentionally
143	 * lossy, following the common human-navigable project-directory convention.
144	 * @param cwd - the session's project directory.
145	 * @returns a single filesystem-safe project directory name.
146	 */
147	export function projectKey(cwd: string): string {
148	  if (cwd.length === 0) throw new Error('cannot encode an empty project path')
149	  let readable = ''
150	  let separatorRun = false
151	  for (let i = 0; i < cwd.length; i++) {
152	    const code = cwd.charCodeAt(i)
153	    const ch = String.fromCharCode(code)
154	    if (ch === '/' || ch === '\\' || ch === ':') {
155	      if (!separatorRun) readable += '-'
156	      separatorRun = true
157	    } else if (ch !== '~' && /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]$/.test(ch)) {
158	      readable += ch
159	      separatorRun = false
160	    } else {
161	      readable += '~' + code.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(4, '0')
162	      separatorRun = false
163	    }
164	  }
165	  const slug = readable.replace(/^-+/, '') || 'root'
166	  return `--${slug.slice(0, 251)}--`
167	}
168	
169	/**
170	 * The configured root's human-navigable project directory. A configured root
171	 * may be local or shared; this grouping does not prescribe its deployment.
172	 * @param root - the backend's session root directory.
173	 * @param cwd - the session's project directory; `undefined` selects `_no-cwd`.
174	 * @returns the project directory path under `root`.
175	 */
176	export function projectDir(root: string, cwd: string | undefined): string {
177	  if (cwd === undefined) return join(root, '_no-cwd')
178	  return join(root, projectKey(cwd))
179	}
180	
181	/**
182	 * The directory owned by one session and available for future session-local
183	 * artifacts.
184	 * @param root - the backend's session root directory.
185	 * @param cwd - the session's project directory.
186	 * @param id - the session id, encoded to one safe path segment.
187	 * @returns the session directory beneath its project directory.
188	 */
189	export function sessionDir(root: string, cwd: string | undefined, id: SessionId): string {
190	  return join(projectDir(root, cwd), encodeSegment(id))
191	}
192	
193	/**
194	 * The append-only event-log file path for a session.
195	 * @param root - the backend's session root directory.
196	 * @param cwd - the session's project directory (`undefined` → `_no-cwd`).
197	 * @param id - the session id, path-encoded via {@link encodeSegment} before filesystem use.
198	 * @param compression - physical artifact encoding and filename suffix.
199	 * @returns the session's configured JSONL artifact path.
200	 */
201	export function logPath(
202	  root: string,
203	  cwd: string | undefined,
204	  id: SessionId,
205	  compression: JsonlCompression,
206	): string {
207	  return join(sessionDir(root, cwd, id), `session${logSuffix(compression)}`)
208	}
209	
210	/**
211	 * Serialize an event batch as JSONL lines (no trailing newline). With
212	 * `packChunks` on, delta-chunk runs pack into `text-chunks` /
213	 * `reasoning-chunks` / `tool-call-chunks` storage rows; off writes one event
214	 * per line, byte-identical to the pre-packing layout. Reading is layout-blind
215	 * either way ({@link scanLog} always decodes rows), so the switch changes only
216	 * newly written bytes.
217	 * @param events - the batch to serialize, in log order.
218	 * @param packChunks - whether to pack delta runs into storage rows.
219	 * @returns the batch's JSONL text; the writer adds the final newline.
220	 */
221	export function eventLines(events: readonly SessionEvent[], packChunks: boolean): string {
222	  const records: readonly StorageRecord[] = packChunks ? packChunkRuns(events) : events
223	  return records.map(record => JSON.stringify(record)).join('\n')
224	}
225	
226	interface SessionLogScan {
227	  meta: SessionHeader
228	  events: SessionEvent[]
229	  committedBytes: number
230	}
231	
232	/** Parse one complete header record supplied independently from event rows. */
233	/**
234	 * Refuse a header carrying a format version this build does not read BEFORE
235	 * validating the current header shape or decoding any event row: a future
236	 * format need not satisfy today's structural checks at all, and its user must
237	 * see "upgrade the harness", never "corrupt session log".
238	 * @param parsed - the JSON-parsed first line of a session artifact.
239	 */
240	function refuseForeignFormatVersion(parsed: unknown): void {
241	  if (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null) return
242	  const { version, id } = parsed as { version?: unknown; id?: unknown }
243	  if (typeof version !== 'number' || version === SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION) return
244	  throw new SessionFormatUnsupportedError(
245	    sessionFormatVersionRefusal(typeof id === 'string' ? id : String(id), version),
246	  )
247	}
248	
249	function parseHeaderRecord(record: Buffer): SessionHeader {
250	  if (record.length === 0 || record.at(-1) !== 0x0A || record.indexOf(0x0A) !== record.length - 1) {
251	    throw new Error('empty or header-less session log')
252	  }
253	  let parsed: unknown
254	  try {
255	    parsed = JSON.parse(record.subarray(0, -1).toString('utf8'))
256	  } catch {
257	    throw new Error('corrupt session log: header line is not valid JSON')
258	  }
259	  refuseForeignFormatVersion(parsed)
260	  if (!isHeaderLine(parsed)) {
261	    throw new Error('corrupt session log: first line is not a session header')
262	  }
263	  return fromHeaderLine(parsed)
264	}
265	
266	/**
267	 * Incrementally scan complete JSONL event records after an independently
268	 * supplied header record. Newline search and byte offsets stay on raw buffers;
269	 * only complete records are decoded to UTF-8. A fragment crossing writes is
270	 * copied because a decoder may reuse its output buffer after `write()` returns.
271	 */
272	export class SessionLogScanner {
273	  private readonly meta: SessionHeader
274	  private readonly events: SessionEvent[] = []
275	  private fragments: Buffer[] = []
276	  private fragmentBytes = 0
277	  private inputBytes: number
278	  private committedBytes: number
279	  private eventLine = 0
280	  private issue: Error | undefined
281	  private finished = false
282	
283	  /**
284	   * Create an event scanner from exactly one newline-terminated header record.
285	   * @param headerRecord - the complete first JSONL record, including its newline.
286	   */
287	  constructor(headerRecord: Buffer) {
288	    this.meta = parseHeaderRecord(headerRecord)
289	    this.inputBytes = headerRecord.length
290	    this.committedBytes = headerRecord.length
291	  }
292	
293	  /**
294	   * Consume the next raw plaintext chunk, retaining only an incomplete final record.
295	   * @param chunk - bytes immediately following all previously supplied bytes.
296	   */
297	  write(chunk: Buffer): void {
298	    if (this.finished) throw new Error('cannot write to a finished session log scanner')
299	    const chunkStart = this.inputBytes
300	    this.inputBytes += chunk.length
301	    let lineStart = 0
302	    for (
303	      let newline = chunk.indexOf(0x0A);
304	      newline !== -1;
305	      newline = chunk.indexOf(0x0A, lineStart)
306	    ) {
307	      const fragment = chunk.subarray(lineStart, newline)
308	      let line = fragment
309	      if (this.fragments.length > 0) {
310	        if (fragment.length > 0) this.fragments.push(fragment)
311	        line = Buffer.concat(this.fragments, this.fragmentBytes + fragment.length)
312	        this.fragments = []
313	        this.fragmentBytes = 0
314	      }
315	      this.consumeEventLine(line, chunkStart + newline + 1)
316	      lineStart = newline + 1
317	    }
318	    if (lineStart < chunk.length) {
319	      const fragment = Buffer.from(chunk.subarray(lineStart))
320	      this.fragments.push(fragment)
321	      this.fragmentBytes += fragment.length
322	    }
323	  }
324	
325	  /**
326	   * Snapshot progress before appending a recoverable torn-frame prefix.
327	   * @returns byte, committed-prefix, and expanded-event cursors.
328	   */
329	  checkpoint(): { inputBytes: number; committedBytes: number; eventCount: number } {
330	    return {
331	      inputBytes: this.inputBytes,
332	      committedBytes: this.committedBytes,
333	      eventCount: this.events.length,
334	    }
335	  }
336	
337	  /**
338	   * Finish scanning, ignoring a final record without a newline as a torn tail.
339	   * @returns the header, contiguous event prefix, and safe truncation offset.
340	   */
341	  finish(): SessionLogScan {
342	    this.finished = true
343	    return { meta: this.meta, events: this.events, committedBytes: this.committedBytes }
344	  }
345	
346	  /** Decode one complete event row and update the contiguous prefix. */
347	  private consumeEventLine(line: Buffer, endByte: number): void {
348	    this.eventLine += 1
349	    let decoded: SessionEvent[]
350	    try {
351	      decoded = decodeStorageRecord(JSON.parse(line.toString('utf8')))
352	    } catch {
353	      this.issue ??= new Error(`corrupt session log: unparsable committed event at line ${this.eventLine}`)
354	      return
355	    }
356	
357	    if (this.issue !== undefined) {
358	      if (decoded.some(event => event.type === 'turn/end')) throw this.issue
359	      return
360	    }
361	
362	    const rowStart = this.events.length
363	    for (const event of decoded) {
364	      if (event.seq !== this.events.length) {
365	        const expected = this.events.length
366	        this.events.length = rowStart
367	        this.issue = new Error(
368	          `corrupt session log: seq gap in committed region at line ${this.eventLine} `
369	          + `(expected ${expected}, got ${event.seq})`,
370	        )
371	        if (decoded.some(candidate => candidate.type === 'turn/end')) throw this.issue
372	        return
373	      }
374	      this.events.push(event)
375	    }
376	    this.committedBytes = endByte
377	  }
378	}
379	
380	/**
381	 * Parse a complete or torn JSONL buffer into its preserved event prefix. This
382	 * compatibility wrapper supplies the first record separately, then delegates
383	 * event rows to {@link SessionLogScanner}.
384	 *
385	 * @param buffer - the raw bytes of the log file (header line first).
386	 * @returns the header, preserved event prefix, and byte offset safe to append at.
387	 */
388	export function scanLog(buffer: Buffer): SessionLogScan {
389	  const headerEnd = buffer.indexOf(0x0A)
390	  if (headerEnd === -1) throw new Error('empty or header-less session log')
391	  const scanner = new SessionLogScanner(buffer.subarray(0, headerEnd + 1))
392	  scanner.write(buffer.subarray(headerEnd + 1))
393	  return scanner.finish()
394	}
395	
396	/**
397	 * Parse just the header line of a log into a {@link SessionHeader}, or
398	 * `undefined` if it is missing/not a header. Used by `list()` to read session
399	 * metadata WITHOUT parsing the whole log: a session picker scales with the
400	 * number of sessions, not the total size of every conversation.
401	 * @param firstLine - the first line of a log file (without its trailing newline).
402	 * @returns the parsed header, or `undefined` when the line is not a well-formed session header.
403	 */
404	export function parseHeaderMeta(firstLine: string): SessionHeader | undefined {
405	  let parsed: unknown
406	  try {
407	    parsed = JSON.parse(firstLine)
408	  } catch {
409	    return undefined
410	  }
411	  if (!isHeaderLine(parsed)) return undefined
412	  return fromHeaderLine(parsed)
413	}

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

</system-reminder>

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * Lossless storage packing for `assistant/chunk` delta runs. Providers stream
3	 * token-sized deltas, so a log stores hundreds of near-identical event lines
4	 * whose JSON envelopes dwarf their payloads (~56× measured on a real DeepSeek
5	 * session). This module packs each run of consecutive same-block delta chunks
6	 * into ONE storage row — `text-chunks`, `reasoning-chunks`, or
7	 * `tool-call-chunks` — and expands rows back to the exact original events.
8	 *
9	 * Storage rows are a durable-encoding vocabulary, NOT session events: they
10	 * never enter `Session.events`, have no `SessionEventMap` entry, and use bare
11	 * (slash-less) type tags so a reader cannot confuse them with the event
12	 * taxonomy (precedent: the JSONL header line's `session` tag). The encoder
13	 * whitelists exact shapes — anything it does not fully recognize is stored
14	 * verbatim, so unknown fields or future chunk variants lose compression, never
15	 * data. The decoder validates before expanding and fails loud on a malformed
16	 * row-tagged value instead of silently dropping a whole run.
17	 *
18	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-session/chunk-rows
19	 */
20	
21	import { CallId, assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
22	import type { StreamChunk } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
23	import type { SessionEvent } from './types.ts'
24	
25	/** The chunk kinds that may pack; block boundaries, usage, and finish chunks always stay one event per line. */
26	type DeltaKind = 'text-delta' | 'reasoning-delta' | 'tool-call-delta'
27	
28	/** A run member: an `assistant/chunk` event whose exact shape the encoder whitelisted. */
29	type DeltaEvent = SessionEvent<'assistant/chunk'>
30	
31	/**
32	 * Fields shared by every packed run: placement, block correlation, and member
33	 * timestamps as gaps. Member `k` reconstructs as seq `seq0 + k` and time
34	 * `time0` plus the first `k` gaps; a gap may be negative when the wall clock
35	 * stepped backwards between events.
36	 */
37	interface RunDataBase {
38	  turn: number
39	  step: number
40	  /** The stream block index every member shares. */
41	  index: number
42	  /** Epoch-ms gaps between consecutive members; length is one less than the member count. */
43	  dt: number[]
44	}
45	
46	/** Payload of a `text-chunks`/`reasoning-chunks` row: one entry per member, never joined — token boundaries are data. */
47	interface TextRunData extends RunDataBase {
48	  texts: string[]
49	}
50	
51	/** Payload of a `tool-call-chunks` row: the run-constant call identity plus each member's raw arguments fragment. */
52	interface ToolCallRunData extends RunDataBase {
53	  id: CallId
54	  /** Present iff every member carried it, with one uniform value (a mixed run never packs). */
55	  name?: string
56	  args: string[]
57	}
58	
59	/**
60	 * A packed run of consecutive delta chunk events, discriminated on `type`.
61	 * `seq0`/`time0` anchor the first member; text and reasoning rows share the
62	 * {@link TextRunData} payload, tool-call rows carry {@link ToolCallRunData}.
63	 */
64	export type ChunkRow =
65	  | { type: 'text-chunks'; seq0: number; time0: number; data: TextRunData }
66	  | { type: 'reasoning-chunks'; seq0: number; time0: number; data: TextRunData }
67	  | { type: 'tool-call-chunks'; seq0: number; time0: number; data: ToolCallRunData }
68	
69	/** One durable log line's JSON value: a session event verbatim, or a packed chunk row. */
70	export type StorageRecord = SessionEvent | ChunkRow
71	
72	/**
73	 * Minimum members before a run packs. Below it a row's envelope rivals the
74	 * event lines it replaces. A format constant, not a tunable: both layouts
75	 * decode identically, so changing it never invalidates stored logs.
76	 */
77	const MIN_RUN = 3
78	
79	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
80	  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null
81	}
82	
83	/** Exact-key check: `value` has every key in `keys` and nothing else. */
84	function hasExactKeys(value: object, keys: readonly string[]): boolean {
85	  return Object.keys(value).length === keys.length && keys.every(k => Object.hasOwn(value, k))
86	}
87	
88	/**
89	 * Classify an event for packing: its delta kind when the ENTIRE shape
90	 * (envelope, data, chunk — exact keys, primitive types, integer seq/time) is
91	 * whitelisted, else `undefined` (store verbatim). Inputs come from live typed
92	 * appends AND parsed fixture files, so the checks are structural, not
93	 * type-trusted. Integer times keep gap encoding exact: a fractional time would
94	 * reconstruct through float subtraction/addition, which need not round-trip.
95	 */
96	function classify(event: SessionEvent): DeltaKind | undefined {
97	  if (event.type !== 'assistant/chunk') return undefined
98	  if (!hasExactKeys(event, ['type', 'seq', 'time', 'data'])) return undefined
99	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(event.seq) || event.seq < 0 || !Number.isSafeInteger(event.time)) return undefined
100	  const data: unknown = event.data

63	
64	/**
65	 * The artefact a program's signatures attest. It names what was signed rather
66	 * than describing what the program runs, so it stays out of the program's
67	 * digest: the same goals signed over two artefacts are one program. Who signed
68	 * comes from the `signoff/recorded` events of the program session, never from
69	 * here.
70	 */
71	export interface ProgramSignoff {
72	  /** Lowercase SHA-256 hex every `signoff/recorded` of this program must carry. */
73	  readonly artefactSha256: string
74	}
75	
76	/**
77	 * How every department of one program is staffed.
78	 *
79	 * `route` is the harness agent the program drives itself through the LLM seam,
80	 * one user turn per attempt. `subagent` delegates each attempt to one child run
81	 * of a registered `ctx.subagents` provider, which writes into the department's
82	 * worktree while the program keeps the checks, the certificate, the caps, and
83	 * the ledger.
84	 */
85	export type ProgramImplementer =
86	  | { readonly kind: 'route' }
87	  | {
88	    readonly kind: 'subagent'
89	    /** Name the provider is registered under on `ctx.subagents`. */
90	    readonly provider: string
91	    /** Display label persisted with a session-backed child, passed through to the provider. */
92	    readonly label?: string
93	  }
94	
95	/** One client deliverable, frozen before its first department starts. */
96	export interface ProgramSpec {
97	  /** What the whole program delivers, stated for a reader of the ledger. */
98	  readonly objective: string
99	  /** Git revision every worktree of the program is created from. */
100	  readonly baseRevision: string
101	  /** The goals the deliverable decomposes into, at least one. */
102	  readonly goals: readonly ProgramGoalSpec[]
103	  /** What the merged head is certified against. */
104	  readonly integration: ProgramIntegrationSpec
105	  /**
106	   * How every department of the program is staffed. A caller may omit it;
107	   * `resolveProgramSpec` materializes `{ kind: 'route' }`, so a
108	   * {@link FrozenProgramSpec} always states one and the digest always covers it.
109	   */
110	  readonly implementer?: ProgramImplementer
111	  /** The artefact the program's signatures attest; required by `requireSignoff`. */
112	  readonly signoff?: ProgramSignoff
113	  /** Input plus output tokens every session of the program may sum to. */
114	  readonly tokenCeiling?: number
115	}
116	
117	/**
118	 * One spec after `resolveProgramSpec` materialized every default it owns. This
119	 * is the form the digest covers, the ledger stores, and the service drives, so
120	 * a reconciliation reads the staffing the program ran under instead of
121	 * re-deriving it.
122	 */
123	export interface FrozenProgramSpec extends ProgramSpec {
124	  readonly implementer: ProgramImplementer
125	}
126	
127	/**
128	 * Status of one goal in its program's ledger.
129	 *
130	 * `pending` has no department yet, `running` has one working, `blocked` waits
131	 * for an operator's resume through the goal domain, `certified` holds a
132	 * certificate over its own branch head, `merged` has that branch inside a
133	 * certified integration, `failed` ended without a certificate, and `abandoned`
134	 * never started because the program ended first.
135	 */
136	export type ProgramGoalStatus =
137	  | 'pending'
138	  | 'running'
139	  | 'blocked'
140	  | 'certified'
141	  | 'failed'
142	  | 'merged'
143	  | 'abandoned'
144	
145	/** How one program ended. */
146	export type ProgramOutcome = 'released' | 'failed' | 'abandoned'
147	
148	/** How the integration of one program stands. */
149	export type ProgramIntegrationStatus = 'running' | 'certified' | 'failed'
150	
151	/** Payload of `program/start`. */
152	export interface ProgramStart {
153	  /** `program-<digest>`, which is also this session's id. */
154	  readonly programId: ProgramId
155	  /** Digest of {@link ProgramStart.spec}, the identity the program runs under. */
156	  readonly specSha256: string
157	  /** The frozen spec, verbatim. */
158	  readonly spec: FrozenProgramSpec
159	  /** Git revision every worktree is created from; the spec's own value, copied for readers of this event alone. */
160	  readonly baseRevision: string
161	  /** How every department is staffed; the spec's own value, copied for readers of this event alone. */
162	  readonly implementer: ProgramImplementer
163	  /** The artefact the program's signatures attest, absent when the deployment does not require one. */
164	  readonly signoff?: ProgramSignoff
165	}
166	
167	/** Payload of `program/goal`. */
168	export interface ProgramGoalRecord {
169	  readonly programId: ProgramId
170	  /** The goal's key in the frozen spec. */
171	  readonly key: string
172	  readonly status: ProgramGoalStatus
173	  /** The department's session, from the first status that has one. */
174	  readonly sessionId?: SessionId
175	  /** Absolute path of the department's worktree, from the first status that has one. */
176	  readonly workspace?: string
177	  /**
178	   * The commit the department branch carried when this status was recorded,
179	   * from `git rev-parse HEAD` in its worktree. A `certified` record states the
180	   * commit its certificate covers, and the integration merges that branch only
181	   * while its head still is this commit.
182	   */
183	  readonly revision?: string
184	  /**
185	   * The tree object {@link ProgramGoalRecord.revision} points at, from
186	   * `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`. Two commits with the same tree deliver the same
187	   * files, so it is what a reader compares when a branch was rewritten.
188	   */
189	  readonly tree?: string

191	  readonly reason?: string
